To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) oil price volatility affects negatively output and investment, (2) financial development mitigates the negative impact of oil price volatility, (3) the effect of financial development on output is stronger when oil prices are volatile, (4) financial development is a necessary condition for the positive effect of oil price on output, and (5) oil price volatility does not affect output volatility in the presence of good financial institutions.
Oil price volatility, a major source of exogenous shocks, has a negative impact on economic growth.
oil price volatility has negative effects on growth in oil rich countries, and that these effects are mitigated by better financial institutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between oil price volatility, financial development and economic growth, and the role of the latter in mitigating the effects of the former on growth.
the role of financial institutions in promoting economic growth and mitigating the effects of output volatility.
the effect of oil prices on growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of financial development in oil rich countries has a significant and positive impact on growth and output volatility.
financial institutions can reduce the volatility of output and mitigate the effect of volatility on growth.
financial development reduces output volatility and mitigates its negative effect on economic growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oil rich countries with better financial institutions are better equipped to deal with the negative effects of oil price volatility, and this is reflected in their higher economic growth.
the quality of financial institutions is an important factor in the ability of oil producing countries to cope with exogenous oil price shocks.
the role of oil prices in growth is not as strong as previously thought, and that the role of finance is more important.

financial institutions are a powerful instrument to mitigate the negative effects of exogenous shocks on growth and development.
financial development is an important tool for economic growth and development.
the quality of financial institutions matters in the presence of exogenous shocks to the economy.
